checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322v1
checked_sources.result: Rechecked primary HTML. Theorem 2.2 gives both E_infty[tau_A]>=A and the stronger local bound P_infty(tau_A<=m)<=m/A. Theorem 3.2 uses a post-change block J0=(T+1):(T+d) and the prefix-crossing block J1=1:(T+d), obtains B_{T,d}=I d{1+o_P(1)}, and proves a polynomial-in-A first-delay miss tail plus an exp(-Omega(T)) macroscopic miss tail. Its deterministic finite stopping bound relies on accumulation over all starts, which the sparse lower-certificate detector does not inherit automatically.

checked_sources.source: Moen 2026, A grid-based methodology for fast online changepoint detection, arXiv:2504.09573v2
checked_sources.result: Rechecked exact grid definition and proof. The published grid has <3 log t points, recycling, and d/2 coverage for every integer d<=t/2. Exact residue coupling implies the stronger 3/5 coverage derived in the predecessor checkpoint.

derived_results.claim: The 3/5 coverage constant derived for Moen's exact two-points-per-dyadic-interval dynamic grid is the best possible uniform constant under the same grid.
derived_results.derivation: Let b=2^(j-2), choose t=11b+1, and d=5b-1. Then r=(t-1) mod 2^(j-1)=b. The consecutive relevant grid points are g_R,j-1=3b and g_L,j=5b, while d<=t/2. Thus the largest retained g<=d is 3b and g/d=3b/(5b-1), which decreases to 3/5 as b grows. Combined with the predecessor proof that every relevant consecutive ratio is at most 5/3, no uniform coverage constant larger than 3/5 can hold for this exact grid.
derived_results.scope: Derived combinatorial property of Moen's explicit grid, not a statement made by the source paper. A denser recycled grid could improve the constant at higher O(K log t) cost.

derived_results.claim: For the sub-Gaussian mean-change case, adding one permanent prefix anchor and using repeated disjoint geometric-grid short-window witnesses closes the rare-tail gap from the predecessor checkpoint: after an ARL-valid deterministic cap, the resulting O(log t)-work/O(log t)-memory lower-certificate detector has a derived late-change CADD upper constant 5/3 relative to the source information scale.
derived_results.construction: Set the target ARL to A and B=ceil(2A), with L=log B. Before the deterministic cap H=B, at every t compute the pathwise-lower pair scores W_{g,t} between the prefix interval 1:t and every trailing g in Moen's recycled G^(t), and stop if their maximum reaches B. Otherwise stop at H. The pair score is the closed-form quadratic balance from the predecessor checkpoint, so it is pathwise no larger than the full Saha-Ramdas D_t(B).
derived_results.false_alarm_proof: Because tau_pair(B)>=tau_full(B), Theorem 2.2's local guarantee gives P_infty(tau_pair(B)<=m)<=m/B. Therefore E_infty[min{tau_pair(B),B}] >= sum_{m=0}^{B-1}(1-m/B)=(B+1)/2>=A. The capped rule is finite on every path while preserving the requested ARL lower bound. Under a changepoint T with log T=o(L), T/L->infinity, also T/B->0, so pre-change stopping probability is o(1).
derived_results.delay_proof: Fix epsilon>0 and D=ceil{(5/3)(1+epsilon)L/I}. For a fixed integer K and attempt times t_j=T+jD, j=1,...,K, the strengthened grid lemma supplies a deterministic trailing g_j in [3D/5,D], so I g_j>=(1+epsilon)L. Since g_j<=D, these K short windows lie in disjoint post-change D-blocks. Pair each short window with the permanent prefix 1:t_j. For fixed K, jD/T->0, so the prefix-versus-short expected mean gap is Delta{1+o(1)} and the long-window kappa term is negligible. Choose eta=eta(epsilon)>0 so small that (1-3eta)^2(1+epsilon)>1. If every prefix average is within eta|Delta| of its expectation and a given short average is within eta|Delta| of nu, then for all large A its pair log-score exceeds L after the o(L) mixture penalty. Hence failure at all K attempts implies either at least one prefix deviation or all K disjoint short-window deviations. Sub-Gaussian concentration yields P(any prefix bad)<=2K exp{-eta^2 I T}=A^{-omega(1)} and, by independence of the disjoint post-change blocks, P(all K short bad)<=2^K exp{-K eta^2(1+epsilon)L}. Choose fixed K with K eta^2(1+epsilon)>1. Then B*P(no stop by T+KD)->0. Already at the first attempt, the miss probability tends to zero, so the expected extra retry cost beyond D is o(D); the deterministic-cap contribution is B*o(1/B)=o(1). Therefore E[(tau-T)^+]<=D{1+o(1)}. Dividing by P(tau>T)>=1-T/B=1-o(1) gives CADD<=D{1+o(1)}. Since epsilon is arbitrary, limsup CADD/(L/I)<=5/3.
derived_results.scope: New derivation, not peer-reviewed and not a theorem in either source. It uses the specific sub-Gaussian quadratic point-null e-process, iid pre/post segments, source late-change conditions, one permanent prefix sufficient statistic, Moen's exact recycled grid, and a fixed epsilon before the asymptotic limit. K may grow rapidly as epsilon is chosen closer to zero, but remains fixed with A for each bound. The result is an upper bound, not a matching lower bound for sparse detectors.
derived_results.importance: This repairs the main weakness in cf-g1-r54: the sparse pathwise-lower detector no longer needs the full all-start accumulation to obtain a finite expected-delay bound. Repeated disjoint short witnesses amplify a merely polynomial first-attempt success guarantee until the cap's rare-event cost is negligible.

candidate_updates.update: Upgrade from high-probability-only 5/3 late-change delay to a derived 5/3 CADD upper constant after adding one permanent prefix anchor, repeated disjoint short-window witness opportunities, threshold B≈2A, and deterministic cap H=B. False-alarm validity remains pathwise inherited from the full e-detector; expected-delay control now comes from retry amplification rather than all-start baseline accumulation.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A single sparse witness plus a deterministic timeout is enough to preserve the 5/3 expected-delay constant.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established and generally too weak: one-shot miss probability is only polynomial in A with an epsilon-dependent exponent that can be below one, so multiplying it by an O(A) cap can dominate expectation.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Use a fixed number of disjoint short-window retries to multiply the miss exponents while sharing one controlled prefix event.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The 3/5 grid factor can be improved without changing Moen's exact grid.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No uniformly. The explicit t=11b+1, d=5b-1 sequence gives best retained ratio 3b/(5b-1)->3/5.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Improving the constant requires a denser/reparameterized grid, not a sharper proof of the same grid.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Re-read the source expected-CADD proof to isolate exactly which all-start term the sparse construction had lost.
Replaced one-shot timeout reasoning with repeated disjoint short-window witnesses against a permanent prefix anchor.
Derived a finite-ARL capped stopping rule and showed retry amplification makes the cap contribution negligible.
Proved the 3/5 coverage constant is sharp for Moen's exact grid rather than merely a loose lower bound.

exact_next_action: Prove a denser recycled grid family with K points per dyadic bucket, including exact wrap-boundary recycling and top-bucket inclusion, then combine its coverage constant with the prefix-retry CADD argument to obtain an explicit O(K log t) compute versus asymptotic delay-constant curve. If recycling fails, pivot to the unknown-variance Gaussian pair certificate rather than weakening validity.
